Subject: Order form redlines — Exhibit B (SKU tiers)

Ben —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement ran the order form past our finance team and legal; attached is our redline for Exhibit B (sku tier matrix + pricing floors/caps). Two quick asks we want to surface before a formal mark-up call:

1) Tier reset trigger: we redlined language to allow a mid-contract tier reset if our monthly usage drops below 65% of target for two consecutive months. We call this a "reset trigger" — need to confirm Redwood's view on operationalizing resets and how they interact with true-ups.

2) Anchoring during true-up: our group wants the floor to re-anchor to whichever side (customer or vendor) is more favorable after each true-up period. Your legal flagged that as problematic.

We've attached: ACME_Redlines_ExhibitB_v3.pdf and the SKU matrix. Please confirm whether Redwood can accept anything close to our proposed language or if you want to propose alternative compromise text. We're trying to close in early June to hit our Q3 onboarding window.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if easier.

—Sarah
Sarah Lim

Acme Health

Sarah —

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the clear asks. I reviewed the attachments and looped in Marissa and Karthik (they're lead AE and pricing ops). Two notes up front:

- We can discuss a pragmatic reset trigger but need to avoid a mechanism that allows retroactive re-anchoring of previously invoiced periods.
- Floor/cap anchoring: Redwood is open to smoothing windows and grace periods; an automatic re-anchor to the "more favorable" side as drafted will create revenue instability for committed capacity.

I'll coordinate a short call with legal if needed. Attached is a working concessions worksheet (internal) — I'll follow up with a consolidated proposed redline that preserves your intent where possible. Can you confirm availability June 8–10 for a 30-min finalization call?

Best,
Ben Carter

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-01T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Order form redlines — internal pricing/legal thoughts

Ben / Karthik —

Read Sarah's redline. My take for a first pass: we should offer a compromise that gives Acme a reset pathway but with bounded mechanics. Proposed bullets to feed legal:

- Replace "re-anchor to more favorable side" with: "re-anchor subject to a 90-day smoothing window; re-anchoring may not move the floor lower than the lowest floor in the preceding 12 months."
- Reset trigger: accept customer-initiated reset after two consecutive months below 65% of target, but reset takes effect prospectively at the next billing period and is subject to a one-time reconciliation true-up to align usage tiers (no retroactive refunds beyond the reconciliation).
- For caps/floors: propose a cap smoothing clause where cap increases are phased over next two billing cycles to avoid step jumps.

Legal will want explicit wording. I've drafted suggested redline text below (paste into reply):

"Tier Reset. Customer may request a Tier Reset if Customer's trailing two months' billable usage falls below 65% of the committed target. A Tier Reset, if accepted by Redwood, shall take effect prospectively at the start of the next billing period and shall be subject to a one-time reconciliation true-up to account for prior over/under usage; such reconciliation will not create retroactive refunds other than credit offsets applied to future invoices.

Anchoring; Smoothing Window. After any reconciliation, the parties shall apply a 90-day smoothing window before any change results in a reduction of the pricing floor. The pricing floor applied after reconciliation shall not be lower than the lowest pricing floor applied during the preceding twelve (12) months.

Cap Phase. Any increase to the pricing cap triggered by usage reclassification shall be phased over the following two billing cycles (50% in first cycle, 50% in second), unless otherwise mutually agreed in writing."

These keep us commercially reasonable while limiting retrospective exposure. Karthik — any concerns from finance?

—Marissa

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@acme-health.com>, David Cho <david.cho@acme-health.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-04T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood proposed redlines — Exhibit B and SKU matrix

Sarah / David —

Thanks again for the redlines. Attached are Redwood's proposed redlines that reflect a compromise around the tier reset and anchoring wording. High-level summary of the changes we propose (see attached PDF for tracked changes):

1) Tier Reset — We accept a customer-requested reset after two consecutive months below 65% usage, but the reset is prospective and subject to a single reconciliation true-up. No retroactive cash refunds; credits allowed against future invoices.

2) Anchoring / Smoothing — We replaced the automatic "more favorable" re-anchor with a 90-day smoothing window and the floor protection clause (cannot re-anchor floor lower than lowest in prior 12 months).

3) Cap Phasing — Any upward cap reclassification is phased over two billing cycles to avoid step-function increases for Acme's budgeting.

We also proposed a minor operational note to the order form: Redwood will publish a one-time usage export for the reconciliation calculation within 10 business days of an agreed reset request; both parties have 14 days to raise calculation disputes before reconciliation is locked.

Attachments included: Redwood_Proposed_ExhibitB_redline.pdf, OrderForm_Schedule_SKU_Matrix.xlsx

If this aligns, we'd like to DocuSign the final order form by June 14 to keep your Q3 start date. Otherwise, please flag specific language you can't live with and we'll tighten. Happy to take 30 minutes on June 9 to walk the wording with legal.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_Proposed_ExhibitB_redline.pdf, OrderForm_Schedule_SKU_Matrix.xlsx

From: David Cho <david.cho@acme-health.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@acme-health.com>, Acme Health Procurement <procurement@acme-health.com>
Date: 2028-06-07T16:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood proposed redlines — Exhibit B and SKU matrix

Ben —

Thanks for the responsiveness and for drafting compromise language. A couple of small asks from legal/finance: 

- Can the smoothing window be 60 days instead of 90? Acme is comfortable with shorter smoothing so long as there is a minimum 60-day notice before a floor reduction applies.
- Please confirm the reconciliation export format (CSV with line-level tokens and timestamps) and that Redwood will retain the reconciliation inputs for 12 months for audit.

One clarification: Sarah noted earlier that Acme wants assurance the floor "will not re-anchor downwards during quarterly true-ups" — your proposed smoothing + 12-month floor floor-protection clause looks like it addresses that, but can you state explicitly in the doc that quarterly true-ups shall not lower a previously-applied floor within its 12-month protection window?

If Redwood can accept those two tweaks, we should be ready to sign. June 9 for a 30-min call works for our counsel — please send an invite.

Regards,
David Cho
Senior Counsel, Acme Health
